A Youth-Led Podcast

Where medicine meets justice.

MedJustice is a youth-led podcast exploring inequalities within healthcare and health education — honest conversations with medical students, clinicians, and advocates working to close the gap.

Listen on Spotify Nominate a guest

The Brief

Health is a right. Access rarely treats it like one.

Hosted by Kaamya and Bhudhav Joshi, MedJustice sits at the intersection of medicine, equity, and social justice. Every episode is a cross-examination of the healthcare system — cultural sensitivity, language barriers, representation in medicine, and who gets left out of "accessible" care.

We talk to the people closest to the problem: medical students, clinicians, and advocates who are actively working to make the system more equitable — and we bring their case to a youth audience that will inherit it.

"Through honest dialogue and youth-driven curiosity, MedJustice aims to inspire a new generation of change."

001 Case Filed
Oct 26, 2025 · 43 min

Equity within Medical Education and Training

Guests: Alia Abiad & Jules Sakowitz — University of Chicago Pritzker School of Medicine

Alia and Jules, med students who came up through Harvard and Stanford, join Kaamya and Bhudhav to unpack equity inside medical training itself — what's working in today's programs, what still needs to change, and what a more culturally aware, accessible future in medicine could look like.
